title: Reproductive System
shortDescription: Male and female reproductive structures, kept strictly biological and educational, with the labelled HD illustration.
genZNote: Creates tomorrow — the one chapter with two separate but parallel structure lists.

illustration.alt: Labelled illustration comparing male and female reproductive structures
illustration.caption: Reproductive System — Cellfie Human Anatomy

structures.name: Epididymis
structures.description: Coiled tube on top of each testis.

structures.name: Vas deferens
structures.function: Carries mature sperm toward the urethra during ejaculation.

structures.name: Seminal vesicle
structures.function: Produces fluid that nourishes sperm, forming part of semen.

structures.name: Prostate gland
structures.description: Gland surrounding the urethra below the bladder.
structures.function: Produces additional fluid that supports sperm.

structures.name: Urethra (male)
structures.description: Shared tube for urine and semen in males.
structures.function: Carries urine or semen out of the body.

structures.name: Ovary
structures.function: Produce eggs (ova) and secrete estrogen and progesterone.

structures.name: Fallopian tube
structures.description: Tube connecting each ovary to the uterus.
structures.function: Site of fertilization; carries the egg toward the uterus.

structures.name: Uterus
structures.function: Site where a fertilized egg implants and develops during pregnancy.

structures.name: Cervix
structures.description: Lower, narrow part of the uterus.
structures.function: Connects the uterus to the vagina; opens during childbirth.

structures.name: Vagina
structures.description: Muscular canal from the cervix to outside the body.
structures.function: Birth canal; receives the penis during intercourse.

comparisons.distinction: Vas deferens carries sperm from the epididymis toward the urethra (male); the fallopian tube carries an egg from the ovary toward the uterus (female) — functionally parallel but structurally distinct.
Ovaries produce eggs and estrogen/progesterone; testes produce sperm and testosterone — the corresponding male and female gonads.

questions.prompt: Where does fertilization normally take place?
questions.explanation: Fertilization normally occurs in the fallopian tube, after which the fertilized egg travels to the uterus to implant.
optionNotes: The egg implants and develops here, but fertilization happens earlier.
Connects the uterus to the vagina, not the fertilization site.
Eggs are released from here, but fertilization happens further along the tube.

questions.prompt: Which structure stores and matures sperm before ejaculation?
questions.explanation: The epididymis, a coiled tube atop each testis, stores and matures sperm before it travels through the vas deferens.
optionNotes: Carries mature sperm, doesn't store/mature it.
Adds nourishing fluid, doesn't store/mature sperm.
Adds fluid to semen, doesn't store/mature sperm.

questions.prompt: In the labelled reproductive illustration, which structure connects the uterus to the vagina?
questions.explanation: The cervix is the lower, narrow part of the uterus that connects it to the vagina.
optionNotes: Connects the ovary to the uterus, not the uterus to the vagina.
Produces eggs, doesn't connect to the vagina.
The uterus itself is the organ above the cervix, not the connector.

sections.heading: Male Reproductive Structures
bullets: Epididymis — stores and matures sperm after production.
Vas deferens — carries sperm from the epididymis toward the urethra.
Seminal vesicle — contributes fluid to semen.
Prostate gland — adds fluid that nourishes and helps transport sperm.
Urethra — carries semen (and, separately, urine) out of the body.
Penis — the external organ through which the urethra opens.

sections.heading: Female Reproductive Structures
bullets: Ovary — produces eggs (ova) and secretes estrogen and progesterone.
Fallopian tube — carries the egg from the ovary toward the uterus; the usual site of fertilization.
Uterus — where a fertilized egg implants and a fetus develops.
Cervix — the narrow lower end of the uterus, opening into the vagina.
Vagina — the muscular canal connecting the cervix to the outside of the body.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The reproductive system consists of the male structures that produce and deliver sperm and the female structures that produce eggs and support pregnancy.
keyFacts: Sperm pathway: testis → epididymis → vas deferens → urethra.
Fertilization normally occurs in the fallopian tube, not the uterus itself.
The prostate and seminal vesicles both add fluid to semen, distinct from sperm production itself.
The cervix is the lower opening of the uterus into the vagina.
commonConfusion: Testis (produces sperm) is often confused with epididymis (only stores/matures sperm, does not produce it).
Fertilization site (fallopian tube) is commonly mistaken for implantation site (uterus) — they are two different steps in two different places.

highYieldFacts: Sperm is produced in the testis, but matured and stored in the epididymis before travelling through the vas deferens.
The egg is normally fertilized in the fallopian tube, then travels to the uterus for implantation.
commonTraps: Don't say the ovary is where fertilization happens — the ovary only releases the egg.
Urethra in males carries both urine and semen (never both at once); this is a frequently tested cross-system fact.
mustRemember: Male path: testis → epididymis → vas deferens → urethra.
Female path: ovary → fallopian tube (fertilization) → uterus (implantation) → cervix → vagina.
